title: Preferences for Advisor Agreement and Accuracy

studies.study_name: Experiment 3B: accurate versus agreeing advisor without feedback

findings.main_hypothesis: The group-level agreeing-advisor pick rate did not differ from chance, despite wide individual differences.

studies.study_name: Experiment 3C: accurate versus agreeing advisor with feedback

findings.main_hypothesis: Participants strongly preferred the accurate advisor, producing a low agreeing-advisor pick rate.
Final estimates were more accurate than initial estimates.

reported_statistics.location: Results, Task accuracy and advice usage

findings.main_hypothesis: Error reduction was substantially larger after accurate advice than after agreeing advice.

reported_statistics.location: Results, Task accuracy and advice usage

required_tests.description: Every unscreened participant completes the original 52-slot sequence: 10 unaided practice trials, 2 practice-advisor trials, two 15-slot familiarisation blocks with attention-check replacements, and one 10-trial advisor-choice block without answer leakage on experimental questions.
Compare agreeing-advisor pick rates in feedback and no-feedback conditions with the reported 0.17 and 0.51 rates.
Compare error reduction after accurate and agreeing advice with the reported directional contrast.

source_limitations: The article combines pilot and preregistered replication data for the continuous Dates Task; participant counts and some pooled analyses therefore have different denominators.
The benchmark reproduces the published behavioral mechanism, not the browser's motor interaction with draggable timeline markers.
The original 10 unaided practice trials, 2 practice-advisor trials, and attention-check termination are implemented from the exact experiment-code commit linked in the paper's S1 File.
Avatar art and unanalysed debrief ratings remain outside the implemented runtime.
The article reports 13.5% reflected-control trials; this published rate is treated as authoritative where historical code snapshots are not self-explanatory.
